issue_context.title: With systemd 252.1-1 one machine has an error output from bootctl status
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd 252.1-1

### Used distribution

Arch Linux

### Linux kernel version used

6.0.8

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

_No response_

### Component

bootctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

I expected no error lines starting Failed to read boot option, when running bootctl status.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

$ sudo bootctl status
Failed to read boot option 8194: No such file or directory
Failed to read boot option 8196: No such file or directory
System:
      Firmware: UEFI 2.70 (INSYDE Corp. 3865.00)
 Firmware Arch: x64
   Secure Boot: disabled (disabled)
  TPM2 Support: yes
  Boot into FW: supported

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Run bootctl status

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_

Do these files show up in output of `ls /sys/firmware/efi/efivars/`?
```
Boot2002-8be4df61-93ca-11d2-aa0d-00e098032b8c
Boot2004-8be4df61-93ca-11d2-aa0d-00e098032b8c
```
Also, can you see their content with `hexdump -C`?
Also, the output of `efibootmgr` would be nice.

Those two lines with Boot2002 and Boot2004 don't appear in the efivars list! The output of the efibootmgr command is:
$ sudo efibootmgr
BootCurrent: 0000
Timeout: 0 seconds
BootOrder: 0000,0001,2001,3000,2002,2004
Boot0000* Linux Boot Manager    HD(1,GPT,07c3f646-6587-4f9e-a84a-f264d55fc6d2,0x800,0x82000)/File(\EFI\systemd\systemd-bootx64.efi)
Boot0001  Windows Boot Manager  HD(1,GPT,07c3f646-6587-4f9e-a84a-f264d55fc6d2,0x800,0x82000)/File(\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\bootmgfw.efi)57494e444f5753000100000088000000780000004200430044004f0042004a004500430054003d007b00390064006500610038003600320063002d0035006300640064002d0034006500370030002d0061006300630031002d006600330032006200330034003400640034003700390035007d00000000000100000010000000040000007fff0400
Boot2001* EFI USB Device        RC
Boot3000* Internal Hard Disk or Solid State Disk        RC

This is nothing particularly concerning then. The EFI boot order var mentions these two boot entries, but those entries don't exist anymore. bootctl is just informing you of that fact.

You should be able to get rid of this with `sudo efibootmgr --bootorder 0,1,2001,3000` (or use a new boot order if you like).

Using the command to remove the last two entries by resetting the boot order, works immediately after that command, and efibootmgr status confirms that, but on rebooting those two errant entries come back and the bootctl command then shows the same original warnings.  Perhaps there is some other way to permanently remove the 2002 and 2004 entries?
Great, thank you. Hopefully this will get into the main branch too.

review_comments: hmm, this should not propagate the error then I guess. i.e. return 0. Also say `, ignoring` as usual
a future use might not do the same, so better to keep returning 0 here to avoid future issues

This is not a library function, but only used in a specific place of bootctl. Hence it is not necessary to consider any future usages.

But, OK, this change is not important for this PR. I will drop it.
